![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/482781bb21d011df5a9140b2b1fb0ebe1108f746c0055077d4f4e9a91fce735d.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $y=\sqrt{2-x},$ $x={y}^{2},$ and the $x$-axis, as shown above. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, we write the second function in terms $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{2-x} \\ {y}^{2} & =2-x \\ x & =2-{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let $f(y)={y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=2-{y}^{2}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ {y}^{2} & =2-{y}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & =1 \\ y & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution corresponding to our region is $y=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/48905a174d688fdb3e099debb7840173a2ce047816003a5be9c089997196f9fb.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=f(y)={y}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=g(y)=2-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y([2-{y}^{2}]-[{y}^{2}])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(2-2{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(y-{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =4\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\text{d}y) \\  & =4\pi ({\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =4\pi ((\frac{1}{2}-0)-(\frac{1}{4}-0)) \\  & =4\pi (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
